newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian FIS leader condemns Paris blast.
newsitem.headline: Algerian FIS leader condemns Paris blast.

text.p: A leader of Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) on Wednesday condemned a bomb attack in Paris that bore striking similarities to blasts last year by militant Algerian Moslems.

"We condemn as strongly as possible...this criminal act which we reject in the most absolute manner because it is an act against innocent people," Rabah Kebir told France 2 television in an interview from Germany where he lives in exile.
The bomb, in a rush-hour train on Tuesday evening, killed two people. Eighty-eight others were treated in hospital for injuries or shock.
The attack was similar to a wave of blasts in 1995 claimed by Algeria's Armed Islamic Group (GIA), more militant in its opposition to the Algiers government than the FIS.
Kebir appealed for an end to bombings against innocent people which he said "neither serve the cause of Algeria nor the cause of Islam. Quite the contrary".
The FIS took up arms against Algiers in 1992 after the military authorities scrapped elections it was poised to win. Some 50,000 people are estimated to have died in the fighting since.

Kebir, who has criticised France for close links with Algiers in the past, said "there has been an evolution in the vision France has of the situation in Algeria. This evolution goes in the direction of finding a peaceful solution, but it is an evolution that is both slow and weak."
